thought.text: Now let me run the full intended ordered sequence in one invocation, as the documented workflow does.

reasoning_content:
The documented `ddev cypress run` runs the specs in order: 01, fachplanung_erstellen, aenderungsantraege. But the specs actually present are 01, 02, 030, 031, 032, 033. The host cypress command references stale spec names. But the setup script deletes ressorts 99/9901. Now let's run the full ordered sequence as intended to validate the complete workflow. Let me run specs in the order 01, 02, 030, 031, 032, 033.

Note the setup script deletes the ressorts, so 01-infrastruktur_setup should now pass. Let me run specs sequentially.

Actually the setup-docu-data script's "partial run" detection depends on argv containing cypress/e2e/ and not 01. When running via docker directly, argv is the cypress command, not the php script. So it's always a "full run" from php's perspective. That means after setup, ressorts 99/9901 are deleted and NOT recreated. So 01-infrastruktur_setup must create them.

Let me run the full ordered sequence in one Cypress invocation.

action.command: cd /workspace; su - ddevuser -c 'cd /workspace && ddev setup-docu-data' >/dev/null 2>&1; docker run --rm --network ddev-tfm-fachplanung_default -e CYPRESS_baseUrl=http://web -e CYPRESS_user_r1=r1_user -e CYPRESS_pass_r1=r1_password -e CYPRESS_user_r2=r2_user -e CYPRESS_pass_r2=r2_password -e CYPRESS_user_r3=r3_user -e CYPRESS_pass_r3=r3_password -v /workspace:/e2e -w /e2e cypress/included:13.17.0 run --spec "cypress/e2e/01-infrastruktur_setup.cy.js,cypress/e2e/02-benutzerverwaltung.cy.js,cypress/e2e/030-fachplanung_erstellen.cy.js,cypress/e2e/031-massnahmen_verwaltung_r3.cy.js,cypress/e2e/032-massnahmen_pruefung_r2.cy.js,cypress/e2e/033-fachplanung_abschliessen_r1.cy.js" 2>&1 | grep -E "✓|✗|passing|failing|Tests:|Passing:|Failing:|Spec Ran" | head -60
